rule: Any tariff returned because a request is made with a provider/eMSP identifier (for example providerId=Shell_RP_2, Shell_RP_1 or Shell_RP) is an eMSP/driver tariff layer unless independent first-party evidence proves it is the CPO's own direct/ad-hoc tariff. Such tariffs must not be used to promote, price, complete or otherwise resolve a CPO in national canonical CPO datasets.
consequences: Do not use Shell_RP_* tariffs for ChargePoint, InstaVolt, bp pulse, TotalEnergies or any other third-party CPO direct pricing.
Do not use providerId tariff coverage percentages as CPO completion evidence.
Keep historical Shell_RP_* reports only as rejected/provenance evidence; they are non-canonical for CPO pricing.
For Shell/ubitricity own-network cases, require independent CPO-direct/ad-hoc evidence before using a price in the CPO layer; providerId alone is insufficient.
Future investigations must stop once the only remaining path yields an eMSP tariff rather than a direct CPO/ad-hoc tariff.
